free_tier.stated: Free users: 2 tunnels, 12 Mbps limit, traffic claimable by daily check-in. [translated from a forum roundup]

egress.terms: Traffic is claimed by daily check-in; no monthly byte figure appears on the home page or in the roundup.; ingress: udp

interface_detail: frpc client plus a documented panel API.
tooling: frpc, Docker image, web panel and an API
chaining: UDP tunnel at 12 Mbps, enough for 1 TiB/month only if the check-in grant is large.
binding_note: The published speed cap would allow about 3.9 TB per month, so the check-in byte grant is the constraint that decides whether 1 TiB is reachable.

identity_cost.detail: Email registration on the panel; the roundup says domestic nodes require real-name verification while overseas nodes do not.

reliability_note: No free-tier reliability statement could be read; the roundup does not report breaks.
confidence_note: console.openfrp.net is a JavaScript shell that returns no text to the reader, so the free-tier table could not be read directly.

evidence.proved: the product supports TCP and UDP tunnels
Tunnel-type table: 'UDP | Bedrock (Geyser) | 19132 | example.com:19132 | CNAME (the port cannot be hidden)' [translated]
'Free users have a clear quota: at most 2 tunnels, 1 GB of traffic per month, 12 Mbps up and down' [translated, third party]

notes: Vendor page confirms UDP carriage but not the free quota. The console is a client-rendered app; reading it needs a browser session, which did not spend.

extras.wg_detail: The vendor home page lists 'TCP / UDP tunnels' as a product feature, which is the transport a WG datagram needs.
extras.volume_stated: No byte figure is published by the vendor. Third-party summaries of the free quota give 2 tunnels, 1.00 GB per month and 12 Mbps; the number is reported, not documented.
